W.note: Lines count 5/7/5 (Mid-win-ter's late dusk; a veil keeps the sun's last light; the sheen of a shell), and nacreous twilight is evoked without being named, with a fairly stock 'veil' and a quiet but unremarkable close.

X.note: Lines count 5/7/5 (Night's edge, pearl-thin cloud; lit from beneath by the sun; seen by no one else), accurately rendering a nacreous cloud lit from below after sunset, and 'seen by no one else' gives the poem its turn.

Y.note: Lines count 5/7/5 (Rare cloud, mother-pearl; blooms where the sky holds no sun; gone before the name), naming mother-pearl and a sunless sky accurately, and 'gone before the name' is the strongest turn in the set despite a blunt opening line.

Z.note: Lines count 5/7/5 (midwinter, the wind; a lens of cloud, not drifting; above the ridge crest), giving a precise lenticular cloud standing over a ridge, with 'not drifting' setting up a quiet tension against the wind though the opener is loose.
